module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 156

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/156](https://www.erdosproblems.com/156)
- [ESS94] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A. and Sós, T., On Sum Sets of Sidon Sets, I. Journal of Number
  Theory (1994), 329-347.
- [Ru98b] Ruzsa, Imre Z., A small maximal Sidon set. Ramanujan J. (1998), 55-58.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Finset Filter

namespace Erdos156

/--
The size of the smallest maximal Sidon set in $\{1, \dots, N\}$.
-/
noncomputable def minMaximalSidonSet (N : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  open scoped Classical in
  sInf (((Icc 1 N).powerset.filter fun (A : Finset ℕ) ↦
    Set.IsMaximalSidonSetIn (A : Set ℕ) N).image card : Set ℕ)

/--
Does there exist a maximal Sidon set $A\subset \{1,\ldots,N\}$ of size $O(N^{1/3})$?

A question of Erdős, Sárközy, and Sós [ESS94].
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_156 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      (fun N ↦ (minMaximalSidonSet N : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun N ↦ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 3 : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem greedySidonSet_isSidon (n : ℕ) : IsSidon (Finset.greedySidonBelow n : Set ℕ) := by
  intro i₁ hi₁ j₁ hj₁ i₂ hi₂ j₂ hj₂ eq
  have subset : Finset.greedySidonBelow n ⊆ (Finset.greedySidon.aux n).1 := Finset.filter_subset _ _
  exact (Finset.greedySidon.aux n).1.2 i₁ (subset hi₁) j₁ (subset hj₁) i₂ (subset hi₂) j₂ (subset hj₂) eq

/--
It is easy to prove that the greedy construction of a maximal Sidon set in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ has size
$\gg N^{1/3}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_156.variants.greedy_lower_bound :
    (fun N ↦ ((Finset.greedySidonBelow N).card : ℝ)) ≫ (fun N ↦ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 3 : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Ruzsa [Ru98b] constructed a maximal Sidon set of size $\ll (N\log N)^{1/3}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_156.variants.ruzsa_upper_bound :
    (fun N ↦ (minMaximalSidonSet N : ℝ)) ≪
      (fun N ↦ ((N : ℝ) * Real.log N) ^ (1 / 3 : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos156

reformulations.difference: The source asks for maximal Sidon sets of size O(N^(1/3)); Lean instead bounds the function giving their minimum cardinality.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every N, the finite family of Sidon subsets of {1,…,N} has an inclusion-maximal member. Consequently the family defining minMaximalSidonSet is nonempty, and its natural-number infimum is attained. Its bound is therefore equivalent to ∃ C > 0, ∃ N₀, ∀ N ≥ N₀, ∃ A, A is maximal Sidon in {1,…,N} and |A| ≤ C N^(1/3). This exact equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean without using the conjecture.

reformulations.difference: Ruzsa's theorem and abstract state existence of a small maximal Sidon set; Lean states the corresponding bound on the minimum cardinality. Ruzsa's final remark also uses this minimum-cardinality formulation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The minimum is attained for every N, so bounding it by C(N log N)^(1/3) is equivalent to existence of a maximal Sidon set satisfying that bound, with a uniform C for all sufficiently large N. The equivalence, including removal of the norms in IsBigO, was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean.

review.notes: Checked all five declarations and the imported Sidon, maximality, greedy-construction, and asymptotic definitions. Lean tests verified minMaximalSidonSet at N = 0,…,5 as 0,1,2,2,2,3; proved that the minimum is attained for every N and positive for N > 0; and checked small greedy sets and their maximality. The lower-bound notation has the correct direction. The logarithm's zero values at N = 0 and 1 are harmless under atTop. The source still marks the main problem open, and both solved variants agree with the cited results. Scratch files compiled successfully; the reviewed file was not modified.
